newsitem.title: UK: British Aerospace up on continued merger talk.
newsitem.headline: British Aerospace up on continued merger talk.

text.p: Shares in British Aerospace Plc were trading at a 12-month high of 12.49-1/2 stg, up 24p by 0945 GMT on continued speculation that the company would merge with another aerospace or defense group by the end of 1997, dealers said.

"There is nothing new in the merger talk," the head of trading at a major brokerage said. "The stock is on a lot of tip sheets for 1997 because people believe it will link-up with someone by the beginning of 1998."
Merger talk intensified after Boeing announced plans to merger with McDonnell Douglas earlier this month.
Analysts believe BAe will eventually need to merge with another group in order to compete against the new U.S. aerospace giant.
BAe had already made repeated calls this year for the continent's aerospace and defence firms to come together to match the might of the new giant U.S. combines such as Lockheed Martin.

In September, senior British Aerospace executives revealed that the company would be prepared to see BAe's own identity dissolved in a series of cross-border mergers by 2002 and analysts say the Boeing-MDC deal should spur on this process.
